name: Tree Reconstruction from Traversals / Uniqueness Determination
recognitionClueHinglish: Do (ya teen) traversal sequences di hain (pre/in/post-order) aur poocha hai tree BANAO, ya poocha hai ye combination tree ko UNIQUELY determine karta hai ya nahi — ye is topic ka sabse bada pattern hai (53 me se 14 PYQs).
whatShouldComeToMind: Inorder + (Preorder OR Postorder) = ALWAYS unique reconstruction possible.
Preorder + Postorder ALONE = NOT unique in general (works only for strictly full/0-or-2-children trees).
Root comes from Preorder's FIRST element or Postorder's LAST element; Inorder splits into left/right subtree sets around that root.
generalSolvingApproach: 1. Identify the root from preorder(first)/postorder(last).
2. Find that root's position in the inorder sequence — everything to its LEFT in inorder is the left subtree's node-set, everything to the RIGHT is the right subtree's.
3. Recurse on each half using the corresponding slice of preorder/postorder.
4. For uniqueness questions (no actual reconstruction needed), just check WHICH pair of traversals is given and apply the rule above.
variationsObserved: Non-standard traversal order defined (e.g., 'New-order': root, right, left) — apply the same reconstruction LOGIC, just adapted to the custom order.
Counting how MANY distinct trees are consistent with a GIVEN single traversal sequence alone (usually many, since one traversal alone is never sufficient).
commonTraps: Assuming preorder+postorder is always sufficient — check if the tree is guaranteed full (0-or-2 children) first.
edgeCases: Tree with only left children or only right children (fully skewed) — preorder alone equals postorder reversed in a special way, worth sanity-checking.

name: Node-Counting Relationships (leaf vs internal vs degree)
recognitionClueHinglish: Poocha hai leaf-node count, ya degree-1/degree-2 node count, given some other count — ye formula/algebra pattern hai (53 me se 12 PYQs), n0=n2+1 jaisी identities ka application.
whatShouldComeToMind: Set up n0+n1+n2=n (total nodes by degree) and n1+2n2=n-1 (edge count) as two equations, solve for whatever's asked.
For trees where EVERY node has 0 or 2 children specifically: n0=n2+1 directly.
conceptsRequired: Tree edge-count identity (n-1 edges for n nodes)
generalSolvingApproach: 1. Write down what's given (leaves? degree-1 count? total nodes?) and what's asked.
2. Set up the two governing equations: n=n0+n1+n2, and n-1=n1+2n2 (edges).
3. Solve algebraically for the unknown — don't try to recall a specific formula for every combination, just re-derive from these two equations each time.
variationsObserved: 'Every node has an odd number of descendants' style indirect constraint — translate into a degree/structure constraint first.
Progressive tree-reduction process (repeatedly removing degree-2 nodes) — track how counts change at each step.
commonTraps: Applying the n0=n2+1 shortcut to a tree that ISN'T guaranteed to have only 0-or-2-degree nodes — re-derive from the general two-equation system instead.

name: Height vs Max/Min Node-Count Bounds
recognitionClueHinglish: Poocha hai given height ke liye maximum/minimum possible nodes kya hain, ya given balance-constraint (weight-balanced, AVL-like) ke saath height ka bound kya hai — ye bound-derivation pattern hai.
whatShouldComeToMind: FIRST check: is height defined by EDGES or NODES on the longest path? This changes every formula by 1.
Max nodes (height h, edge-definition) = 2^(h+1)-1 (perfect tree). Min nodes = h+1 (skewed chain).
For balance-constrained trees (weight-balanced, size-balanced), height bound is typically Θ(log n) — derive via the constraint's recursive shrinkage ratio.
generalSolvingApproach: 1. Confirm the height definition (edges vs nodes) stated in the question.
2. For max/min WITHOUT balance constraints: apply 2^(h+1)-1 and h+1 directly (adjusting for the definition).
3. For balance-constrained trees: set up a recurrence for minimum-nodes-at-height-h based on the constraint's shrinkage ratio, solve it.
variationsObserved: Weighted external path length computation (sum of leaf-depth × leaf-weight) — a specific numeric application rather than a pure bound.
commonTraps: Mixing edge-height and node-height definitions mid-problem — pick one and stay consistent.

name: Array Representation of Complete Binary Tree (index formulas)
recognitionClueHinglish: Complete binary tree ko array me store kiya gaya hai (1-indexed ya 0-indexed), aur poocha hai parent/child index formula, ya kisi element ka LEVEL kya hoga — ye index-arithmetic pattern hai.
whatShouldComeToMind: 1-indexed: parent(i)=⌊i/2⌋, left(i)=2i, right(i)=2i+1. Shift by 1 for 0-indexed arrays.
generalSolvingApproach: 1. Confirm whether the array is 1-indexed or 0-indexed (check the question's stated starting index).
2. Apply the corresponding parent/child formula directly.
3. For level questions, use ⌊log2(index)⌋ (1-indexed) as the starting point.
commonTraps: Using the 1-indexed formula on a 0-indexed array or vice versa.

name: Recursive Code Tracing on Tree Structures
recognitionClueHinglish: Ek recursive C function di hai jo tree pointers (left/right) pe operate karti hai, aur poocha hai return value/output/time-complexity kya hoga — ye Recursion topic ka tree-specific extension hai.
whatShouldComeToMind: Same call-tree tracing skill as the Recursion topic — draw the actual tree, resolve recursive calls bottom-up from leaves (NULL base case).
generalSolvingApproach: 1. Draw the specific tree given (or implied) in the question.
2. Trace the recursive function starting from leaves/NULL nodes upward, exactly as in the Recursion topic.
3. For complexity questions, count total node-visits (usually O(n) for a single full traversal) unless the recursion revisits nodes.
variationsObserved: Function counting subtrees with a specific property (like exactly k nodes) — needs careful bottom-up size tracking, not just a simple traversal.
commonTraps: Not handling the NULL base case correctly when tracing by hand.

name: Balanced Tree Definitions & Rebalancing Operations
recognitionClueHinglish: AVL/size-balanced tree ki definition di hai, aur poocha hai insert ke baad balance-factor kya hoga, ya rebalancing steps kya honge — ye balanced-tree-operation pattern hai (introductory level, deeper AVL content lives in the dedicated AVL Tree topic).
whatShouldComeToMind: Balance factor = height(left subtree) - height(right subtree); AVL requires this ∈ {-1,0,1} at every node.
After insertion, only ancestors of the inserted node can have their balance factor change — check bottom-up from the insertion point.
conceptsRequired: Basic rotation intuition (deep coverage in AVL Tree topic)
generalSolvingApproach: 1. Insert as in a normal BST first.
2. Walk back up from the inserted node to the root, updating heights/balance-factors.
3. At the first node found unbalanced, apply the appropriate rotation (see AVL Tree topic for rotation specifics).
commonTraps: Checking balance only at the root instead of at every ancestor of the inserted node.

name: Structure-Preserving Design (deletion procedures, node counting by structure, conceptual TRUE/FALSE)
recognitionClueHinglish: Poocha hai ek deletion procedure design karo jo tree STRUCTURE preserve kare, ya kitne distinct binary trees possible hain n nodes se, ya BFS/DFS visiting-order comparison — ye broader design/conceptual pattern hai.
whatShouldComeToMind: Number of distinct tree SHAPES with n nodes = Catalan number.

'Preserve structure' deletion in a complete-tree-like structure usually means: replace deleted node with the LAST node in level-order, then re-heapify/re-balance if needed (same idea as heap deletion).
BFS vs DFS visiting order comparisons need explicit small-tree simulation, not abstract reasoning.
generalSolvingApproach: 1. For counting-distinct-trees questions, recall/derive the Catalan number for the given n.
2. For deletion-procedure questions, think 'replace with last-level-order node, then fix up' as the general template.
3. For BFS-vs-DFS-order questions, simulate both explicitly on a small concrete tree.
variationsObserved: Expected distance between two randomly chosen leaves (probability + tree-structure combined).
Assigning n distinct values to an unlabeled tree shape to form a valid BST — count ways (usually exactly 1 way per shape, since BST order is forced by the values).
commonTraps: Assuming any arbitrary node can replace a deleted node while preserving a specific structural invariant (complete/balanced) — usually only the LAST level-order node works cleanly.
